active_layer_usage.QIF Core: Represent Quality Intent, risk, loss boundary, evidence, verdict, confidence, uncertainty, acceptance gates, and governance triggers.
active_layer_usage.QIF Discovery Layer: Discover candidate Quality Intents before QIF artifacts are authored by using concern sources, loss-boundary exploration, solution-bias discovery, boundary-confusion discovery, concept-comprehension discovery, and failure-oriented discovery patterns.
active_layer_usage.AOF Integration: Map AOF runtime commands, benchmark results, release gates, work artifacts, and council evidence into QIF-governed quality claims.
active_layer_usage.QIF Guided Elicitation Runtime: Help users who do not know QIF terminology express candidate quality knowledge through schema-backed, verifier-backed guided elicitation packages, raw-answer preservation, teach-back confirmation, and low-confidence governance routing.

layer_model.current_executable_baseline: QIF v0.5.4 adds an executable guided-elicitation package type with schema, verifier, example package, and retained negative fixtures. AOF adopts it as an external provider capability for quality-intent discovery and operator elicitation guidance, while the active AOF quality package .aof/quality/QIFPKG-AOF-V5-001.json remains the local machine-readable AOF baseline until AOF explicitly maps the guided elicitation package into runtime commands.

compatibility.semantic_truth_boundary: QIF validator and profile compatibility checks can prove structure, traceability, reference resolution, confidence reproducibility, and rule compliance. They do not prove semantic truth, market truth, expert correctness, or operator comprehension.

not_allowed: Do not vendor QIF schemas or docs into AOF as the source of truth.
Do not claim QIF validator pass proves semantic quality truth.
Do not treat tests, artifact count, actor count, dashboard existence, or release tags as quality by themselves.
Do not upgrade QIF compatibility silently without recording the selected provider profile.
Do not treat QIF v0.5.4 guided elicitation verifier pass as proof of semantic truth, user consent, expert correctness, or best possible questioning.

upgrade_policy.aof_upgrade_requirement: When QIF changes version, AOF must add or update a qif-provider-profile artifact, record compatibility boundaries, and run governance review before using the new profile for quality claims.
upgrade_policy.fallback: If the selected QIF version cannot be validated or mapped, AOF may continue using the last active provider profile but must mark new quality claims as profile-stale or governance-review-required.

governance.review_trigger: Trigger review when QIF version, source tag, Discovery Layer boundary, adapter outputs, confidence policy, or semantic truth boundary changes.
governance.acceptance_gate: AOF quality claims must reference the active QIF provider profile and must explain which claims are structural, runtime-backed, operator-validated, externally validated, or not proven.
